content: 1. Atazanavir reduces the effects of metformin, potentially due to insulin resistance caused by protease inhibitors. Monitor blood glucose levels closely and use caution when co-administering these drugs. 2. Atazanavir increases methadone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor patients closely for signs of increased methadone effects and adjust the dose if necessary. 3. Atazanavir significantly increases methylergonovine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to potentially serious adverse effects. Co-administration is contraindicated. Use alternative therapies. 4. Atazanavir increases methylprednisolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for corticosteroid-related side effects and adjust the dose as needed. 5. Methylprednisolone may reduce atazanavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 6. Atazanavir enhances the effects of metoprolol through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Consider lowering the beta-blocker dose and monitor closely. 7. Metronidazole may increase atazanavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but monitoring is advised. 8. Miconazole (vaginal) may increase atazanavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 9. Atazanavir increases midazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to prolonged sedation. Co-administration is contraindicated. Use alternative sedatives. 10. Intranasal midazolam co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors like atazanavir can result in higher systemic exposure and prolonged sedation. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 11. Atazanavir increases midostaurin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. If unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions, especially during the first week of treatment. 12. Atazanavir increases mifepristone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed 300 mg/day of mifepristone for Cushing’s syndrome when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor for increased toxicity. 13. Mifepristone may increase atazanavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely for adverse effects. 14. Atazanavir reduces the effects of miglitol, potentially due to insulin resistance caused by protease inhibitors. Monitor blood glucose levels closely and use caution. 15. Co-administration of mipomersen and atazanavir may increase hepatic enzyme levels. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs) closely and use caution. 16. Atazanavir increases mirvetuximab soravtansine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Monitor closely. 17. Mitotane decreases atazanavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for reduced efficacy of atazanavir and adjust the dose if necessary. 18. Atazanavir increases modafinil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 19. Atazanavir increases mometasone (inhaled) levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of Cushing’s syndrome or adrenal suppression. Monitor closely and use caution. 20. Atazanavir increases mometasone (intranasal) levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and use caution. 21. Atazanavir increases montelukast levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 22. Atazanavir enhances the effects of nadolol through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Consider lowering the beta-blocker dose and monitor closely. 23. Atazanavir increases naldemedine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for potential adverse effects when co-administered with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 24. Atazanavir significantly increases naloxegol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, which may precipitate opioid withdrawal symptoms. Co-administration is contraindicated. 25. Atazanavir reduces the effects of nateglinide, potentially due to insulin resistance caused by protease inhibitors. Monitor blood glucose levels closely and use caution. 26. Atazanavir enhances the effects of nebivolol through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Consider lowering the beta-blocker dose and monitor closely. 27. Nefazodone increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Use alternative therapies. 28. Atazanavir increases nelfinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs may increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Monitor closely. 29. Atazanavir increases neratinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 30. Atazanavir increases netupitant/palonosetron levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely, but no dosage adjustment is required. 31. Atazanavir and nevirapine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Monitor closely and consider alternative therapies. 32. Atazanavir increases nicardipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and use caution. 33. Atazanavir increases nifedipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely, but the clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 34. Atazanavir increases nilotinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely, but the clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 35. Atazanavir increases nimodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely, but the clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 36. Nirmatrelvir increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for increased adverse effects and adjust therapy as needed. 37. Atazanavir increases nirogacestat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 38. Atazanavir increases nisoldipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and use caution. 39. Atazanavir increases nitrendipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely, but the clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 40. Nizatidine decreases atazanavir levels by increasing gastric pH, reducing atazanavir solubility and plasma concentrations. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 41. Atazanavir may increase or decrease norethindrone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and consider alternative contraceptives. 42. Atazanavir increases norgestrel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of adverse effects. Monitor closely and use caution. 43. Atazanavir increases nortriptyline levels through an unspecified mechanism. Monitor closely and use caution. 44. Atazanavir increases olaparib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or reduce the olaparib dose if unavoidable. 45. Atazanavir increases oliceridine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust the dose as needed. 46. Atazanavir increases omaveloxolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or reduce the omaveloxolone dose if unavoidable. 47. Atazanavir increases ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir & dasabuvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 48. Omeprazole decreases atazanavir levels by increasing gastric pH, reducing atazanavir solubility and plasma concentrations. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 49. Atazanavir increases ondansetron levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely, but no dosage adjustment is recommended. 50. Orlistat decreases atazanavir levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, potentially leading to loss of virological control in HIV-infected patients. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently and discontinue orlistat if viral load increases. 51. Atazanavir increases osilodrostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the osilodrostat dose by half and monitor closely. 52. Atazanavir increases osimertinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies.
